connectivity.title: Connection problem detected
connectivity.healthy: Your connection looks fine. Nothing below reports a problem.
connectivity.nothingToReceive: Nobody else is in the room, so there is nothing to receive.
connectivity.pending: Still setting up the connection. The steps below turn green as they complete.
connectivity.hint.candidates: No local network address could be found. A VPN or virtual network adapter is the usual cause.
connectivity.hint.stun: The media server is not answering. A firewall is most likely blocking UDP traffic to it.
connectivity.hint.icePath: No usable network path to the server. UDP is probably blocked, so a TURN relay over TCP or TLS is needed.
connectivity.hint.dtls: The network path works but the encryption handshake did not finish. A proxy or security appliance may be filtering DTLS.
connectivity.hint.outbound: Your audio and video are not leaving this device. An outgoing firewall rule is the usual cause.
connectivity.hint.inbound: No audio or video is arriving. Incoming media is most likely being blocked upstream of this device.
problem.uplink: Your upload is saturated. Turning off your camera or screen share helps.
problem.downlink: Your download is saturated. Stopping incoming video relieves it.
problem.cpu: This device is out of processing power. Closing other applications helps.
problem.capture: Your camera or microphone stopped delivering media. Check the device.
problem.loss: Your network is losing packets. Another network may work better.
problem.sending: What others receive from you is poor.
peer.noMediaArriving: No audio or video is arriving from {displayName}
quality.explanation.blocky-video: The picture is coarsely compressed, so it looks blocky or smeared. The sender is not getting enough bandwidth for this resolution.
quality.explanation.choppy-video: Frames arrive unevenly, so motion stutters even though video is still flowing.
quality.explanation.dropped-video-frames: Decoded frames are being thrown away before they reach the screen, usually because this device cannot keep up.
quality.explanation.frozen-video: The picture has stopped updating while the track is still live.
quality.explanation.volatile-fps: The time between frames keeps changing, which shows up as uneven, jerky motion.
quality.explanation.audio-jitter-buffer-: The jitter buffer is stretching and compressing audio to cope with irregular arrival, which distorts the sound.
quality.explanation.invented-speech: The decoder is filling gaps with invented audio because packets are missing, which sounds robotic or warbly.
quality.explanation.synthesized-audio: Part of the audio being played was synthesized to cover lost packets rather than actually received.
quality.explanation.downscaled-screensha: The screen share is being sent at a much lower resolution than it is captured at, so text will look soft.
quality.explanation.encoder-bottleneck: The video encoder cannot keep up with the capture rate, so frames are dropped before they are sent.
quality.explanation.high-deviation-from-: Much less video is being sent than the encoder is aiming for, typically a sign of a constrained uplink.
quality.explanation.video-capture-bottle: The camera or capture pipeline is delivering fewer frames than requested.
quality.explanation.silent-audio-source: The microphone is producing silence. It may be muted at the OS level or captured from the wrong device.
quality.explanation.dry-inbound-track: The track is subscribed but no media is arriving at all.
quality.explanation.dry-outbound-track: The track is being produced but no media is leaving this device.
quality.explanation.stuck-decoder: Data is arriving but the decoder has stopped producing frames from it.
quality.explanation.transport-delay-degr: Round trip time has risen and stayed high, which adds noticeable delay to the conversation.
quality.explanation.transport-loss-susta: Packets are being lost continuously rather than in short bursts.
quality.explanation.unstable-transport: The network path keeps changing quality, so quality will fluctuate.
quality.explanation.uplink-congestion: More data is being sent than the upload can carry, so the sender is being throttled.
quality.explanation.downlink-congestion: More data is arriving than the download can carry, so incoming media is being cut back.
quality.explanation.av-desync: Audio and video have drifted apart, so lips no longer match the sound.
quality.explanation.audio-playout-synthe: Audio playout is being synthesized to cover missing packets.
quality.explanation.blocked-inbound-medi: Incoming media appears to be blocked by a firewall or proxy.
quality.explanation.blocked-outbound-med: Outgoing media appears to be blocked by a firewall or proxy.
quality.explanation.blocked-stun-request: STUN requests are not getting through, so the connection cannot discover a network path.
quality.explanation.cpulimitation: This device is short on CPU, so media quality is being reduced to keep the call running.
quality.explanation.decoder-bottleneck: Frames are arriving faster than this device can decode them.
quality.explanation.dtls-handshake-faile: The media connection could not be secured, so media cannot flow.
quality.explanation.dtls-handshake-stall: Securing the media connection is taking unusually long.
quality.explanation.frame-assembly-stall: Packets are arriving but no longer add up to complete video frames.
quality.explanation.ice-connection-faile: No usable network path to the server could be established.
quality.explanation.ice-disconnected: The network path to the server dropped and is being re-established.
quality.explanation.ice-establishment-fa: Setting up the network path to the server failed.
quality.explanation.ice-transport-stalle: The network path is up but has stopped responding.
quality.explanation.inbound-video-playou: Video is being decoded but not shown at the expected rate, so playback lags behind what was received.
quality.explanation.no-available-ice-can: No reachable network address was found for this connection.
quality.explanation.pixelated-video: The picture is heavily compressed for the size it is displayed at, so it looks pixelated.
quality.explanation.rtp-sender-stalled: The sender has stopped transmitting media on this connection.
quality.explanation.transport-demux-stal: Media is arriving but can no longer be sorted onto its tracks.
quality.explanation.unstable-ice-path: The network path keeps switching, which interrupts media.
quality.explanation.video-decoder-overlo: Decoding takes longer than the time available per frame, so video falls behind.
quality.explanation.video-flow-disrupted: Incoming video is no longer flowing smoothly - it is choppy or frozen.
quality.explanation.video-recovery-faile: Video stalled and repeated requests for a fresh keyframe have not recovered it.
quality.explanation.capture-source-lost: The camera or screen being captured has gone away.
quality.explanation.capture-track-muted: The captured track has been muted by the system.

label.managementservice.rulesHelpKinds: There are two kinds of rule. An Access rule decides who may sign in. A Grant rule decides what someone gets once they are in.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpSteps: Allow rules broaden, Block rules narrow. First add Allow rules for the groups of people who should get in, then Block rules for anyone inside those groups who should not.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpCloses: To admit only the people you list, add a Block rule with the comparison "matches anyone". It applies to everyone no other rule mentions, so your Allow rules become the guest list.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpBlock: The most specific matching rule wins. Naming an exact address beats a rule about a group, so you can block a whole provider and still admit one address from it. If two rules are equally specific, Block wins.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpOpen: A tenant is open by default: anyone the login provider offers can sign in unless a Block rule stops them.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpAdmins: Administrators are never refused. You, the other admins and owners of this tenant, and the super admin can always sign in, so a mistake here cannot lock you out of your own settings.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpGrant: A Grant rule gives a matching user a group membership or an admin role. It is applied at every sign in, so a user who starts matching it later still gets it.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpGrantKe: Grants are only ever added, never taken away. Someone who stops matching a Grant rule, or whose rule you delete, keeps what they were already given until you remove it by hand.
label.managementservice.rulesHelpGrantAc: Grant rules do not let anyone in. Someone refused by the Access rules never reaches them, so a Grant rule is no substitute for an Allow rule.

label.managementservice.roomLockedToolti: When enabled, new unmanaged rooms start in a locked state. Only the first user to join who is authenticated (logged in via SSO/management) can bypass the lock and admit others from the lobby. All other users, including subsequent authenticated users, will be placed in the lobby.

label.managementservice.botPolicyTooltip: A bot is a headless browser page that records, streams or transcribes a room. Disabled: no bots. Access token only: a bot needs one of the tokens below, from an allowed address, and then also enters locked and meetings-only rooms. All bots: bots without a token are admitted too, like ordinary participants.

label.managementservice.botApiUrlTooltip: The https address of the provider service for this kind of job, as given by the provider. Moderators can then start and stop the job from the room. Leave the job type, this address and the key empty for a bot that is started by hand.

label.managementservice.botTokenShownOnc: Generate a token and copy it into the bot's configuration now: only its hash is saved, and the token cannot be shown again. If it is lost, delete this entry and create a new one.
